newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Swiecie paper firm sale seen Jan or Feb '97.
newsitem.headline: Polish Swiecie paper firm sale seen Jan or Feb '97.

text.p: Polish Zaklady Celulozy i Papieru w Swieciu Celuloza SA, one of the two largest paper firms in Poland, is likely to be privatised in January or February 1997, a member of the firm's management board said.

Zofia Mytych told Reuters the treasury ministry has already shortlisted prospective investors for the 65-percent stake in the firm, but had yet to decide whether it would first sell the stake or place 15-percent shares on the Warsaw bourse.

"I think in January or February the 65-percent stake will be sold ... and our issue prospectus is already in the Polish Securities Commission so we could be ready to enter the bourse in January as well," she said.
"There is a shortlist of several investors bidding for the 65-percent stake," she added, but declined to give their names.
She said the remaining 15 percent of the shares would be earmarked for employees and five percent for a planned fund to meet claims for property confiscated under communism.

She also said the company, which would be one of the largest on the Warsaw Exchange, did not plan to carry out a new share issue before entering the bourse as the firm did not need additional capital.
"We are not planning a new share issue as recent years have been financially very good," she said.

The company, which has 25 percent of the Polish paper market, expected its net profit to amount to 80 million zlotys on 714-million-zloty sales in 1996, down from last year's 110 million-zloty-net and 760 million-zloty-sales.
Mytych said that according to a preliminary forecast for 1997 the firm saw its earnings flat at 80 million zlotys of net profit and 720-million-zloty-sales.
